sentences.text: jane : Hello, Jane Fairbanks speaking.
sentences.zh: jane : 你好，我是简·费尔班克斯。

sentences.text: frank : Oh, good morning.
sentences.zh: frank : 哦，早上好。

sentences.text: My name's Frank Pritchard.
sentences.zh: 我的名字是弗兰克·普里查德。

sentences.text: I've just retired and moved to Southoe.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚退休，搬到了索斯欧。

sentences.text: I'd like to become a volunteer, and I gather you co-ordinate voluntary work in the village.
sentences.zh: 我想成为一名志愿者，听说您负责协调村里的志愿工作。

sentences.text: jane : That's right.
sentences.zh: jane : 没错。

sentences.text: frank : What sort of thing could I do?
sentences.zh: frank : 我能做些什么工作呢？

sentences.text: jane : Well, we need help with the village library.
sentences.zh: jane : 嗯，我们需要人手协助村图书馆的工作。

sentences.text: We borrow books from the town library, and individuals also donate them.
sentences.zh: 我们从镇上的图书馆借书，个人也会向我们捐赠图书。

sentences.text: So, one thing you could do is get involved in collecting them – if you've got a car, that is.
sentences.zh: 因此，您可以参与图书收集工作——前提是您有车。

sentences.text: frank : Yes, that's no problem.
sentences.zh: frank : 是的，这完全没问题。

sentences.text: jane : The times are pretty flexible so we can arrange it to suit you.
sentences.zh: jane : 时间安排非常灵活，我们可以根据您的情况来协调。

sentences.text: Another thing is the records that we keep of the books we're given, and those we borrow and need to return to the town library.
sentences.zh: 另一项工作是整理我们所收到图书的记录，以及我们借阅后需归还给镇图书馆的图书记录。

sentences.text: It would be very useful to have another person to help keep them up to date.
sentences.zh: 再增加一名人员来协助更新这些记录将非常有用。

sentences.text: frank : Right.
sentences.zh: frank : 明白了。

sentences.text: I'm used to working on a computer – I presume they're computerised?
sentences.zh: 我习惯使用电脑——我猜这些记录都是电脑化的吧？

sentences.text: jane : Oh yes.
sentences.zh: jane : 哦，是的。

sentences.text: frank : Is the library purpose-built?
sentences.zh: frank : 这个图书馆是专门建造的吗？

sentences.text: I haven't noticed it when I've walked round the village.
sentences.zh: 我在村里散步时好像没注意到它。

sentences.text: jane : No, we simply have the use of a room in the village hall, the West Room.
sentences.zh: jane : 不是的，我们只是使用村礼堂里的一间房间，即西厅。

sentences.text: It's on the left as you go in.
sentences.zh: 您进门后左边就是。

sentences.text: frank : I must go and have a look inside the hall.
sentences.zh: frank : 我得去礼堂里面看看。

sentences.text: jane : Yes, it's a nice building.
sentences.zh: jane : 是的，那是一座很漂亮的建筑。

sentences.text: frank : Do you run a lunch club in the village for elderly people?
sentences.zh: frank : 村里是否为老年人开设午餐俱乐部？

sentences.text: I know a lot of places do.
sentences.zh: 我知道很多地方都有这样的俱乐部。

sentences.text: jane : Yes, we have a very successful club.
sentences.zh: jane : 是的，我们的俱乐部办得非常成功。

sentences.text: frank : I could help with transport, if that's of any use.
sentences.zh: frank : 如果需要的话，我可以帮忙提供交通服务。

sentences.text: jane : Ooo definitely.
sentences.zh: jane : 哦，当然需要！

sentences.text: People come to the club from neighbouring villages, and we're always in need of more drivers.
sentences.zh: 参加俱乐部的人来自周边村庄，我们一直急需更多司机。

sentences.text: frank : And does the club have groups that focus on a particular hobby, too?
sentences.zh: frank : 那么，俱乐部是否也设有专注于特定爱好的小组呢？

sentences.text: I could get involved in one or two, particularly if there are any art groups.
sentences.zh: 我可以参加一两个，尤其是如果有美术类小组的话。

sentences.text: jane : Excellent.
sentences.zh: jane : 太好了。

sentences.text: I'll find out where we need help and get back to you.
sentences.zh: 我会查清楚哪些地方需要帮助，然后尽快联系您。

sentences.text: frank : Fine.
sentences.zh: frank : 好的。

sentences.text: What about help for individual residents.
sentences.zh: 那么，针对个别居民的帮助呢？

sentences.text: Do you arrange that at all?
sentences.zh: 您会安排这类服务吗？

sentences.text: jane : Yes, we do it as a one-off.
sentences.zh: jane : 是的，我们提供一次性帮助。

sentences.text: In fact, there's Mrs Carroll.
sentences.zh: 事实上，卡罗尔夫人目前就有需求。

sentences.text: She needs a lift to the hospital next week, and we're struggling to find someone.
sentences.zh: 她下周需要去医院，而我们正难以找到合适的人选送她。

sentences.text: frank : When's her appointment?
sentences.zh: frank : 她的预约时间是什么时候？

sentences.text: jane : On Tuesday.
sentences.zh: jane：星期二。

sentences.text: It would take the whole morning.
sentences.zh: 这会占用整个上午。

sentences.text: frank : I could do that.
sentences.zh: frank：我可以做这件事。

sentences.text: jane : Oh, that would be great.
sentences.zh: jane：哦，那太好了。

sentences.text: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.text: And also, next week, we're arranging to have some work done to Mr Selsbury's house before he moves, as he isn't healthy enough to do it himself.
sentences.zh: 另外，下周我们打算在塞尔兹伯里先生搬入之前，为他的房子做一些修缮工作，因为他身体不够健康，无法自己完成。

sentences.text: We've got some people to decorate his kitchen, but if you could do some weeding in his garden, that would be wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我们已安排了一些人来粉刷他的厨房，但如果你能在他的花园里除草，那就太棒了。

sentences.text: frank : OK.
sentences.zh: frank：好的。

sentences.text: I'd enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意做这件事。

sentences.text: And presumably the day and time are flexible.
sentences.zh: 而且，日期和时间应该是可以灵活安排的吧？

sentences.text: jane : Oh yes.
sentences.zh: jane：哦，是的。

sentences.text: Just say when would suit you best, and we'll let Mr Selsbury know.
sentences.zh: 你只需告诉我们你什么时候最方便，我们会通知塞尔兹伯里先生。

sentences.text: frank : Good.
sentences.zh: frank：好的。

sentences.text: jane : The volunteers group also organises monthly social events, which is a great way to meet other people, of course.
sentences.zh: jane：志愿者小组还每月组织一次社交活动，当然，这也是结识其他人的绝佳方式。

sentences.text: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 Audioscripts frank : Uhuh.
sentences.zh: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 音频脚本 frank：嗯哼。

sentences.text: jane : So next month, on the 19th of October, we're holding a quiz – a couple of residents are great at planning unusual ones, and we always fill the village hall.
sentences.zh: jane：因此，下个月，也就是10月19日，我们将举办一场知识问答比赛——有几位居民特别擅长策划别出心裁的问答活动，我们每次都能把村礼堂坐满。

sentences.text: frank : That sounds like fun.
sentences.zh: frank：听起来很有趣。

sentences.text: Can I do anything to help?
sentences.zh: 我能帮上什么忙吗？

sentences.text: jane : Well, because of the number of people, we need plenty of refreshments for halfway through.
sentences.zh: jane：由于参加人数较多，我们需要准备大量茶点，供活动进行到一半时享用。

sentences.text: So, if you could provide any, we'd be grateful.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能提供一些，我们将不胜感激。

sentences.text: frank : I'm sure I could.
sentences.zh: frank：我肯定可以。

sentences.text: I'll think about what to make, and let you know.
sentences.zh: 我会考虑一下做什么，然后告诉你。

sentences.text: jane : Thank you.
sentences.zh: jane：谢谢。

sentences.text: Then on November the 18th, we're holding a dance, also in the village hall.
sentences.zh: 接着，11月18日，我们将在村礼堂举办一场舞会。

sentences.text: We've booked a band that specialises in music of the 1930s – they've been before, and we've had a lot of requests to bring them back.
sentences.zh: 我们已预订了一支专长于20世纪30年代音乐的乐队——他们之前来过，而且我们收到了很多要求再次邀请他们的呼声。

sentences.text: frank : I'm not really a dancer, but I'd like to do something to help.
sentences.zh: frank：我其实不太会跳舞，但我很想帮忙做些事情。

sentences.text: jane : Well, we sell tickets in advance, and having an extra person to check them at the door, as people arrive, would be good – it can be quite a bottleneck if everyone arrives at once!
sentences.zh: jane：嗯，我们提前售票，如果能在人们入场时多安排一个人在门口检票，那就很好了——因为如果大家同时到达，门口很容易出现拥堵！

sentences.text: frank : OK, I'm happy with that.
sentences.zh: frank：好的，我很乐意承担这项工作。

sentences.text: jane : We're also arranging a New Year's Eve party.
sentences.zh: jane：我们还在筹备一场新年除夕派对。

sentences.text: We're expecting that to be a really big event, so instead of the village hall, it'll be held in the Mountfort Hotel.
sentences.zh: 预计这将是一场规模盛大的活动，因此地点不再设在村礼堂，而是改在蒙特福特酒店。

sentences.text: frank : The …?
sentences.zh: frank：……？

sentences.text: jane : Mountfort.
sentences.zh: jane：蒙特福特。

sentences.text: M-O-U-N-T-F-O-R-T Hotel.
sentences.zh: M-O-U-N-T-F-O-R-T 酒店。

sentences.text: It isn't in Southoe itself, but it's only a couple of miles away.
sentences.zh: 它并不在索斯欧镇内，但距离那里只有几英里远。

sentences.text: The hotel will be providing dinner and we've booked a band.
sentences.zh: 酒店将提供晚餐，我们也已预订了一支乐队。

sentences.text: The one thing we haven't got yet is a poster.
sentences.zh: 目前唯一还没落实的是海报。

sentences.text: That isn't something you could do, by any chance, is it?
sentences.zh: 不知你是否碰巧能帮忙设计一张？

sentences.text: frank : Well actually, yes.
sentences.zh: frank：实际上，可以的。

sentences.text: Before I retired I was a graphic designer, so that's right up my street.
sentences.zh: 我退休前是一名平面设计师，所以这正合我意。

sentences.text: jane : Oh perfect!
sentences.zh: jane：哦，太完美了！

sentences.text: I'll give you the details, and then perhaps you could send me a draft …
sentences.zh: 我来给您详细说明一下，然后您或许可以发一份草稿给我……

sentences.text: frank : Of course.
sentences.zh: frank：当然可以。

sentences.text: Good morning, and welcome to Oniton Hall, one of the largest estates in the area.
sentences.zh: 早上好，欢迎来到奥尼顿庄园，这是本地区最大的庄园之一。

sentences.text: My name's Nick, and I'm one of the guides.
sentences.zh: 我叫尼克，是这里的导游之一。

sentences.text: I'll give you a brief introduction to the estate while you're sitting down, and then we'll walk round.
sentences.zh: 在各位就座时，我先为大家简要介绍一下这座庄园，之后我们再一起参观。

sentences.text: The estate consists of the house, gardens, parkland and farm, and it dates back to the fourteenth century.
sentences.zh: 这座庄园包括主宅、花园、公园和农场，其历史可追溯至十四世纪。

sentences.text: The original house was replaced in the late seventeenth century, and of course it has had a large number of owners.
sentences.zh: 最初的宅邸于十七世纪晚期被重建，当然，它历经了众多主人。

sentences.text: Almost all of them have left their mark, generally by adding new rooms, like the ballroom and conservatory, or by demolishing others .
sentences.zh: 几乎每一位主人都留下了他们的印记，通常是通过增建新房间（如舞厅和温室），或拆除其他房间。

sentences.text: The farm looks much as it's always done, although the current owner has done a great deal of work to the flower beds.
sentences.zh: 农场外观基本保持原貌，尽管现任主人对花坛进行了大量修整。

sentences.text: In the seventeenth century, the estate was owned by a very wealthy man called Sir Edward Downes.
sentences.zh: 十七世纪时，庄园由一位名叫爱德华·唐斯爵士的非常富有的人士拥有。

sentences.text: His intention was to escape from the world of politics, after years as an active politician, and to build a new house worthy of his big collection of books, paintings and sculptures.
sentences.zh: 他原本是一位活跃的政治家，多年从政后，意图远离政界，并建造一座配得上其庞大藏书、绘画及雕塑收藏的新宅邸。

sentences.text: He broke off contact with his former political allies, and hosted meetings of creative and literary people, like painters and poets.
sentences.zh: 他中断了与昔日政治盟友的联系，并主办各类创意及文学人士聚会，例如画家与诗人。

sentences.text: Unusually for his time, he didn't care whether his guests were rich or poor, as long as they had talent.
sentences.zh: 在他那个时代，这实属罕见——他并不在意宾客是否富有或贫穷，只要他们具备才华即可。

sentences.text: Big houses like Oniton had dozens of servants until the 1920s or 30s, and we've tried to show what their working lives were like.
sentences.zh: 像奥尼顿这样的大型宅邸，直至二十世纪二三十年代仍雇有数十名仆人；我们努力还原了他们当时的工作生活状况。

sentences.text: Photographs of course don't give much of an idea, so instead, as you go round the house, you'll see volunteers dressed up as nineteenth-century servants, going about their work.
sentences.zh: 照片当然难以充分展现，因此，在您参观宅邸时，会看到身着十九世纪仆人服饰的志愿者，正从事各自的工作。

sentences.text: They'll explain what they're doing, and tell you their recipes, or what tools they're using.
sentences.zh: 他们会向您解释自己正在做的事情，并分享他们的食谱或所使用的工具。

sentences.text: We've just introduced this feature to replace the audio guide we used to have available.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚推出这一特色项目，以取代原先提供的语音导览。

sentences.zh: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129

sentences.text: ed : Did you make notes while you were watching the performances of Romeo and Juliet , Gemma?
sentences.zh: ed：吉玛，观看《罗密欧与朱丽叶》演出时，你做笔记了吗？

sentences.text: gemma : Yes, I did.
sentences.zh: gemma：是的，我做了。

sentences.text: I found it quite hard though.
sentences.zh: 不过我觉得挺难的。

sentences.text: I kept getting too involved in the play.
sentences.zh: 我总是过于沉浸于戏剧本身。

sentences.text: ed : Me too.
sentences.zh: ed：我也是。

sentences.text: I ended up not taking notes.
sentences.zh: 结果我根本没做笔记。

sentences.text: I wrote down my impressions when I got home.
sentences.zh: 回家后才写下自己的观感。

sentences.text: Do you mind if I check a few things with you?
sentences.zh: 我可以跟你核对几处细节吗？

sentences.text: In case I've missed anything.
sentences.zh: 以防我遗漏了什么。

sentences.text: And I've also got some questions about our assignment.
sentences.zh: 另外，我对我们的作业还有一些问题。

sentences.text: gemma : No, it's good to talk things through.
sentences.zh: gemma：没问题，讨论一下很好。

sentences.text: I may have missed things too.
sentences.zh: 我也可能遗漏了一些内容。

sentences.text: ed : OK great.
sentences.zh: ed：好的，太好了。

sentences.text: So first of all, I'm not sure how much information we should include in our reviews.
sentences.zh: 那么首先，我不太确定我们的剧评中该包含多少信息。

sentences.text: gemma : Right.
sentences.zh: gemma：嗯。

sentences.text: Well, I don't think we need to describe what happens.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们无需描述剧情发展。

sentences.text: Especially as Romeo and Juliet is one of Shakespeare's most well-known plays.
sentences.zh: 尤其是《罗密欧与朱丽叶》本就是莎士比亚最广为人知的剧作之一。

sentences.text: ed : Yeah, everyone knows the story.
sentences.zh: ed：是啊，大家都知道这个故事。

sentences.text: In an essay we'd focus on the poetry and Shakespeare's use of imagery etc., but that isn't really relevant in a review.
sentences.zh: 在论文中，我们会聚焦于诗歌语言及莎士比亚的意象运用等，但这些在剧评中并不相关。

sentences.text: We're supposed to focus on how effective this particular production is.
sentences.zh: 我们应着重分析此次特定制作的效果如何。

sentences.text: gemma : Mmm.
sentences.zh: gemma：嗯。

sentences.text: We should say what made it a success or a failure.
sentences.zh: 我们应该指出是什么使其成功或失败。

sentences.text: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 Audioscripts ed : And part of that means talking about the emotional impact the performance had on us.
sentences.zh: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 音频脚本 ed：而这其中一部分意味着谈论演出对我们产生的情感影响。

sentences.text: I think that's important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很重要。

sentences.text: gemma : Yes.
sentences.zh: gemma：是的。

sentences.text: And we should definitely mention how well the director handled important bits of the play – like when Romeo climbs onto Juliet's balcony.
sentences.zh: 而且我们当然应该提到导演如何处理剧中的关键片段——比如罗密欧爬上朱丽叶阳台的那一幕。

sentences.text: ed : And the fight between Mercutio and Tybalt .
sentences.zh: ed：还有墨丘利奥与提伯尔特之间的打斗。

sentences.text: gemma : Yes.
sentences.zh: gemma：是的。

sentences.text: It would also be interesting to mention the theatre space and how the director used it but I don't think we'll have space in 800 words.
sentences.zh: 另外，提及剧场空间以及导演如何运用它也会很有趣，但我认为800字的篇幅里恐怕没有空间容纳这部分内容。

sentences.text: ed : No.
sentences.zh: ed：不会（有空间）。

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.text: That all sounds quite straightforward.
sentences.zh: 这一切听起来相当直接明了。

sentences.text: ed : So what about The Emporium Theatre's production of the play?
sentences.zh: ed：那么，埃姆波里乌姆剧院的这版《罗密欧与朱丽叶》呢？

sentences.text: gemma : I thought some things worked really well but there were some problems too.
sentences.zh: gemma：我觉得有些方面效果非常好，但也存在一些问题。

sentences.text: ed : Yeah.
sentences.zh: ed：是啊。

sentences.text: What about the set, for example?
sentences.zh: 比如说布景怎么样？

sentences.text: gemma : I think it was visually really stunning.
sentences.zh: gemma：我认为它在视觉上确实非常震撼。

sentences.text: I'd say that was probably the most memorable thing about this production.
sentences.zh: 我可以说，这大概就是本场演出最令人难忘的部分。

sentences.text: ed : You're right.
sentences.zh: ed：你说得对。

sentences.text: The set design was really amazing, but actually I have seen similar ideas used in other productions.
sentences.zh: 布景设计确实非常出色，但事实上，我在其他几场演出中也见过类似的设计理念。

sentences.text: gemma : What about the lighting?
sentences.zh: gemma：灯光效果呢？

sentences.text: Some of the scenes were so dimly lit it was quite hard to see.
sentences.zh: 有些场景的灯光实在太暗，以至于很难看清。

sentences.text: ed : I didn't dislike it.
sentences.zh: ed：我并不反感这种处理方式。

sentences.text: It helped to change the mood of the quieter scenes .
sentences.zh: 它有助于改变那些安静场景的情绪氛围。

sentences.text: gemma : That's a good point.
sentences.zh: gemma：这是个很好的观点。

sentences.text: ed : What did you think of the costumes?
sentences.zh: ed：你对服装怎么看？

sentences.text: gemma : I was a bit surprised by the contemporary dress, I must say.
sentences.zh: gemma：坦白说，我对采用当代服饰感到有点意外。

sentences.text: ed : Yeah – I think it worked well, but I had assumed it would be more conventional.
sentences.zh: ed：是啊——我觉得这种处理效果不错，但我原本以为会更传统一些。

sentences.text: gemma : Me too.
sentences.zh: gemma：我也是。

sentences.text: I liked the music at the beginning and I thought the musicians were brilliant, but I thought they were wasted because the music didn't have much impact in Acts 2 and 3.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢开场时的音乐，也觉得乐手们非常出色；但我觉得他们被浪费了，因为第二幕和第三幕的音乐几乎没产生什么影响。

sentences.text: ed : Yes – that was a shame.
sentences.zh: ed：是啊——这确实挺可惜的。

sentences.text: gemma : One problem with this production was that the actors didn't deliver the lines that well.
sentences.zh: gemma：这场演出的一个问题是演员台词表现不够好。

sentences.text: They were speaking too fast.
sentences.zh: 他们语速太快了。

sentences.text: ed : It was a problem I agree, but I thought it was because they weren't speaking loudly enough – especially at key points in the play.
sentences.zh: ed：这个问题确实存在，我同意；不过我认为原因在于他们声音不够响亮——尤其是在全剧的关键节点上。

sentences.text: gemma : I actually didn't have a problem with that.
sentences.zh: gemma：实际上，我倒没觉得这是个问题。

sentences.text: ed : It's been an interesting experience watching different versions of Romeo and Juliet , hasn't it?
sentences.zh: ed：观看不同版本的《罗密欧与朱丽叶》真是一次有趣的体验，不是吗？

sentences.text: gemma : Definitely.
sentences.zh: gemma：绝对是。

sentences.text: It's made me realise how relevant the play still is.
sentences.zh: 它让我意识到这部戏剧至今仍具有很强的现实意义。

sentences.text: ed : Right.
sentences.zh: ed：没错。

sentences.text: I mean a lot's changed since Shakespeare's time, but in many ways nothing's changed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，自莎士比亚时代以来，许多事情都已改变，但在很多方面却依然如故。

sentences.text: There are always disagreements and tension between teenagers and their parents.
sentences.zh: 青少年与父母之间始终存在着分歧与紧张关系。

sentences.text: gemma : Yes, that's something all young people can relate to – more than the violence and the extreme emotions in the play.
sentences.zh: gemma：是的，这一点所有年轻人都能感同身受——其共鸣程度甚至超过了剧中暴力与极端情绪所引发的反应。

sentences.text: ed : How did you find watching it in translation?
sentences.zh: ED: 你觉得看翻译版的感受如何？

sentences.text: gemma : Really interesting.
sentences.zh: GEMMA: 非常有趣。

sentences.text: I expected to find it more challenging, but I could follow the story pretty well.
sentences.zh: 我原本以为会更难理解，但其实我能相当清楚地跟上剧情。

sentences.text: ed : I stopped worrying about not being able to understand all the words and focused on the actors' expressions.
sentences.zh: ED: 我不再纠结于无法听懂所有单词，而是专注于演员的表情。

sentences.text: The ending was pretty powerful.
sentences.zh: 结尾部分非常震撼。

sentences.text: gemma : Yes.
sentences.zh: GEMMA: 是的。

sentences.text: That somehow intensified the emotion for me .
sentences.zh: 这反而让情感体验对我而言更加强烈了。

sentences.text: ed : Did you know Shakespeare's been translated into more languages than any other writer?
sentences.zh: ED: 你知道莎士比亚是被译成语言种类最多的作家吗？

sentences.text: gemma : What's the reason for his international appeal, do you think?
sentences.zh: GEMMA: 你认为他为何具有如此广泛的国际吸引力呢？

sentences.text: ed : I was reading that it's because his plays are about basic themes that people everywhere are familiar with.
sentences.zh: ED: 我读到过，原因在于他的戏剧探讨的是世界各地人们都熟悉的普遍主题。

sentences.text: Right, everyone, let's make a start.
sentences.zh: 好了，各位，我们开始吧。

sentences.text: Over the past few sessions, we've been considering the reasons why some world languages are in decline, and today I'm going to introduce another factor that affects languages, and the speakers of those languages, and that's technology and, in particular, digital technology.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几次课中，我们一直在探讨某些世界性语言衰落的原因；而今天，我将介绍另一个影响语言及其使用者的因素——即科技，尤其是数字技术。

sentences.text: In order to illustrate its effect, I'm going to focus on the Icelandic language, which is spoken by around 321,000 people, most of whom live in Iceland – an island in the North Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 为说明其影响，我将以冰岛语为例展开讲解。冰岛语目前约有32.1万人使用，其中绝大多数居住在北大西洋海域的冰岛岛上。

sentences.text: The problem for this language is not the number of speakers – even though this number is small.
sentences.zh: 这种语言面临的问题并非使用者人数——尽管这一数字确实很小。

sentences.text: Nor is it about losing words to other languages, such as English.
sentences.zh: 同样，问题也不在于从其他语言（如英语）中流失词汇。

sentences.text: In fact, the vocabulary of Icelandic is continually increasing because when speakers need a new word for something, they tend to create one, rather than borrowing from another language.
sentences.zh: 事实上，冰岛语词汇量正持续增加，因为当使用者需要表达新概念时，通常倾向于自行创造新词，而非借用其他语言的词汇。

sentences.text: All this makes Icelandic quite a special language – it's changed very little in the past millennium, yet it can handle twenty-first-century concepts related to the use of computers and digital technology.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素使得冰岛语成为一种极为特殊的语言——它在过去一千年中变化极小，却仍能自如表达与计算机及数字技术相关的二十一世纪概念。

sentences.text: Take, for example, the word for web browser … this is vafri in Icelandic, which comes from the verb ‘to wander'.
sentences.zh: 以‘网络浏览器’一词为例……冰岛语中称为‘vafri’，源自意为‘漫游’的动词。

sentences.text: I can't think of a more appropriate term because that's exactly what you do mentally when you browse the internet.
sentences.zh: 我想不出比这更贴切的术语了，因为浏览互联网时，你的思维状态恰恰就是漫游。

sentences.text: Then there's an Icelandic word for podcast – which is too hard to pronounce!
sentences.zh: 再比如冰岛语中表示‘播客’的词——发音实在太难了！

sentences.text: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.text: Icelandic, then, is alive and growing, but – and it's a big but – young Icelanders spend a great deal of time in the digital world and this world is predominantly English.
sentences.zh: 因此，冰岛语依然充满活力且不断发展；但——这是一个非常关键的转折——年轻一代冰岛人花费大量时间沉浸于数字世界，而这个数字世界主要以英语为主导。

sentences.text: Think about smartphones.
sentences.zh: 试想一下智能手机。

sentences.text: They didn't even exist until comparatively recently, but today young people use them all the time to read books, watch TV or films, play games, listen to music, and so on.
sentences.zh: 直到相对近期，智能手机才问世；而如今，年轻人频繁使用它们来读书、观看电视或电影、玩游戏、听音乐等等。

sentences.text: Obviously, this is a good thing in many respects because it promotes their bilingual skills, but the extent of the influence of English in the virtual world is staggering and it' s all happening really fast.
sentences.zh: 显然，从许多方面来看，这是一件好事，因为它有助于提升他们的双语能力；但英语在虚拟世界中的影响力之大令人震惊，而且这一切正以惊人的速度发生。

sentences.text: For their parents and grandparents, the change is less concerning because they already have their native-speaker skills in Icelandic.
sentences.zh: 对他们的父母和祖父母而言，这种变化带来的担忧较小，因为他们已具备母语级别的冰岛语能力。

sentences.text: But for young speakers – well, the outcome is a little troubling.
sentences.zh: 但对于年轻使用者来说——结果则略显令人忧虑。

sentences.text: For example, teachers have found that playground conversations in Icelandic secondary schools can be conducted entirely in English, while teachers of much younger children have reported situations where their classes find it easier to say what is in a picture using English, rather than Icelandic .
sentences.zh: 例如，教师发现，冰岛中学操场上学生之间的对话可能完全使用英语进行；而面向更年幼儿童的教师则报告称，课堂上孩子们往往觉得用英语描述图片内容比用冰岛语更容易。

sentences.text: The very real and worrying consequence of all this is that the young generation in Iceland is at risk of losing its mother tongue.
sentences.zh: 这一切所导致的一个真实且令人担忧的后果是：冰岛年轻一代正面临丧失母语的风险。

sentences.text: Of course, this is happening to other European languages too, but while internet companies might be willing to offer, say, French options in their systems, it's much harder for them to justify the expense of doing the same for a language that has a population the size of a French town, such as Nice.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种情况也正在其他欧洲语言中发生；但尽管互联网公司或许愿意为其系统提供法语等选项，要让他们为使用人口仅相当于法国尼斯市规模的语言投入同等资源，则很难证明其合理性。

sentences.text: The other drawback of Icelandic is the grammar, which is significantly more complex than in most languages.
sentences.zh: 冰岛语的另一劣势在于其语法，其复杂程度显著高于大多数语言。

sentences.text: At the moment, the tech giants are simply not interested in tackling this.
sentences.zh: 目前，科技巨头对此根本毫无兴趣去攻克。

sentences.text: So, what is the Icelandic government doing about this?
sentences.zh: 那么，冰岛政府正在采取什么措施呢？

sentences.text: Well, large sums of money are being allocated to a language technology fund that it is hoped will lead to the development of Icelandic sourced apps and other social media and digital systems, but clearly this is going to be an uphill struggle.
sentences.zh: 目前，政府正拨出巨额资金设立语言技术基金，希望借此推动开发基于冰岛语的应用程序及其他社交媒体和数字系统；但显然，这将是一场艰难的攻坚战。

sentences.text: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 Audioscripts On the positive side, they know that Icelandic is still the official language of education and government.
sentences.zh: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 听力原文稿 从积极角度看，他们深知冰岛语仍是教育和政府事务的官方语言。

sentences.text: It has survived for well over a thousand years and the experts predict that its future in this nation state is sound and will continue to be so.
sentences.zh: 冰岛语已存续一千多年以上，专家预测，它在该主权国家的未来前景稳固，且将持续保持稳固。

sentences.text: However, there's no doubt that it's becoming an inevitable second choice in young people's lives.
sentences.zh: 然而，毫无疑问的是，它正不可避免地退居为年轻人生活中的第二选择。

sentences.text: This raises important questions.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一些重要问题。

sentences.text: When you consider how much of the past is tied up in a language, will young Icelanders lose their sense of their own identity ?
sentences.zh: 当你想到历史的诸多层面都深深植根于一种语言之中时，冰岛的年轻人是否会因此失去自身的身份认同感？

sentences.text: Another issue that concerns the government of Iceland is this.
sentences.zh: 冰岛政府关注的另一个问题是这个。

sentences.text: If children are learning two languages through different routes, neither of which they are fully fluent in, will they be able to express themselves properly?
sentences.zh: 如果儿童通过不同途径学习两种语言，而对这两种语言都未能达到完全流利的程度，他们能否恰当地表达自己？
